Heard Mr. Himanshu Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Sakib Ahmed, learned
Panel Lawyer for the State/respondents.

2.  By this petition under Section 528 of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the petitioner has prayed for the following relief(s):
"(i)That the Hon'ble court may kindly be pleased to direct the respondent authorities to produce the entire record pertaining to the case of petitioner.
(ii) That this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to quash the FIR bearing FIR No.
590 registered against the present Petitioner in P.S. Supela, District Durg, C.G. u/s 388, 384, 506 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 as well as Charge sheet No.334/2022 and all consequent criminal proceedings in light of justice and equity.
(iii) That, the order dated 12/03/2024 of charge framing under Section 384, 388 and 506 r/w 34 of IPC passed in criminal case no RCC 5193/2022 may be quashed in the interest of justice.
(iv) To quash the order dated 27/05/2022 by which cognizance of the offence was taken by the Ld trial Court in the criminal case bearing No. RCC 5193/2022.

(v)That this Hon'ble court may further be pleased to pass any other order in favor of petitioner as it may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case with cost."
3. The facts, in brief, as projected by the petitioner is that an FIR bearing No. 590/2021 was registered under Section 388, 506 read with 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short, the IPC) on 27.07.2021 bearing Crime No. 0/2021 at Police Chowki, Smriti Nagar, Police Station, Supela,
District Durg, on the complaint of one Kamal Sen wherein it has been alleged that the co-accused,
namely, Gurjindar Pal Singh, while posted as Inspector General of Police, Raipur Range had given assurance to complainant's wife through present petitioner that he would not let the challan to be filed in 60 days in FIR No. 195/15, dated 23.04.2015 registered against the complainant so that he may be entitled for default bail.
The said FIR was later renumbered as Crime No. 590/2021 at Police Station, Supela.
The matter was investigated by the police and final report bearing No. 334/2022 was submitted before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Durg on 23.05.2022.

The learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Durg, took cognizance of the matter vide order dated 27.05.2022 and thereafter, vide order dated 12.03.2024, charges were framed against him for the offences under Section 506 Part II,
388/34 and 384/34 of the IPC.
The petitioner abjured the guilt and prayed for trial.
4. Mr. Himanshu Pandey, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the allegations levelled against the petitioner are false, baseless and malicious.
There is no material to connect the petitioner with the offence in question.

Further, the most important aspect of the matter is that the Ranjit Singh Saini vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22652290/
2 incident is alleged to have occurred six years ago and the FIR has been lodged against the petitioner and the co-accused persons after an inordinate delay of six years for which there is no explanation.

sentences.text: The petitioner is in no manner connected with the crime in question and the entire criminal proceedings deserves to be quashed.

The main allegation is against the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh, who was posted as the then Inspector General of Police, Raipur Range who would assist in not letting the final report of the police submitted before the learned trial Court so that the complainant-Kamal Kumar Sen may get default bail and for that purpose, an illegal gratification was demanded.

The co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh also had challenged the registration of the aforesaid FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings against him vide Cr.M.P. No. 1488/2023 wherein this Hon'ble Court had been pleased to allow the said petition and quash the FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings so far it related to him vide order dated 13.11.2024.

5. Mr. Pandey further submits that the complainant/respondent No. 5 himself is an accused in FIR No. 195/2015 registered at Police Station, Mahasamund for the offences under Sections 467, 468,
471, 420, 120B of IPC registered on 23.04.2025 wherein it has been alleged that a tanker bearing No. CG/04/HQ/4745 which was carrying 28000 liters of furnace oil was changed and kept in Shubam Organic Industrial area Birkoni, Mahasamund and substituted with inferior quality of furnace oil.

Just after the arrest of the respondent No.5/complainant Kamal Sen on 25.06.2016,
co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh was transferred to Police Headquarters, Raipur, 11.07.2016.
Therefore, there was no occasion to give such assurance to the complainant by the present petitioner because the co- accused was no more the supervisory officer for exercising any authority over the concerned Police Station.

Further it is a matter of record that complainant-Kamal Kumar Sen who is complainant of instant FIR No. 590/2021, was released on bail by this Hon'ble Court vide order was dated 13.02.2017 in MCRC No. 260/2017 only after depositing amount of Rs. 8,16,299/- in the competent court.
Moreover.
matter was pending before the competent criminal court, therefore there was no question of giving such assurance either by the present petitioner or co-accused.
There is no material on record to show that there is any connection or acquaintance of the petitioner with Gurjindar Pal Singh or the complainant Kamal Kumar Sen.
The petitioner is a member of Rotary International and was a District Governor of Rotary International District No 3261 in 2019-2020 (part of Odisha, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh).
Therefore, by virtue of that post he was inviting various dignitaries into his social welfare events organized under the banner of Rotary club.

As the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh was one of the esteemed and reputed officer of the District as well as awardee of President's Police Medal and Police Medal for Gallantry, he was also invited as Chief Guest in one of the events organized by the Rotary Club while the petitioner was the District Governor when he had an opportunity of meeting with the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh.
The petitioner came to know about the above registration of the above said FIR from the local newspaper in which his name was mentioned.
Thereafter, petitioner was called by certain police officers and the concerned Police Station many times and was asked about the incident narrated in the above said FIR.

In the police statement, the petitioner categorically denied either knowing the complainant or about the allegation of exchange of any money between the complainant and the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh, through him.
However, the police officers tried to convince the petitioner that the above said case was between the State and Gurjindar Pal Singh, therefore, the petitioner should support the State.
Further, he was assured that if the petitioner testifies the incident as narrated above, he would be spared or else he would have to face the adverse consequences.

However,

3 petitioner stood his ground by stating the truth, as no such incident as narrated in the above said FIR had ever taken place, but under threat of torture, the present petitioner was forced to sign on some blank papers, affidavit, register and stamp papers.
6.

sentences.text: Mr. Pandey further submits that the concerned police officials called one witness Bhaskar Mudliyar (who is known to the petitioner) in connection with the present FIR wherein he had submitted that, in June, 2016 the complainant called him on phone and sought his help in the case in which he was arrested.
Thereafter, he approached the present petitioner to enquire whether he could help the complainant which was refused by the petitioner as the matter was pending in the concerned Court.
Bhaskar Mudliar, in his statement to the Police also denied having any knowledge about exchange of money between Gurjindar Pal Singh and complainant through the petitioner.
It was revealed by him that he was also forced to sign on various blank papers affidavit, register and stamp papers .

7. It is submitted by Mr. Pandey that in view of the aforesaid factual background, the aforesaid FIR alongwith all the consequential criminal proceedings are liable to be quashed as firstly, the FIR was lodged after a delay of about 6 years which is one of the important fact to be considered while registration of the FIR.

The entire sequence of events leading to the registration of the FIR unequivocally demonstrates that it is actuated by mala fides and a part of a well thought out strategy to somehow send the petitioner behind the bars.
The allegations pertain to year 2015-2016 and the complaint was made in the year 2021 and that too, at Police Chowki, Smriti Nagar.

Immediately after receiving the complaint without even conducting any preliminary enquiry into the allegations and seeking any explanation for such an inordinate delay of more than 6 years, the FIR has been registered.

8. Mr. Pandey lastly submits that in a petition filed by Gurjindar Pal Singh, being Cr.M.P. No.
1488/2023 and who is the co-accused in the present case, this Hon'ble Court, vide order dated 13.11.2024 has quashed the FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings, which is sought to be challenged herein and as such, the same relief may also be extended to the petitioner herein.
9.

On the other hand, Mr. Sakib Ahmed, learned Panel Lawyer appearing for the State/respondent submits that once a complaint is lodged and a congnizable offence is made out, the Police is bound to register the FIR and investigate the matter.

The police has already completed the investigation and filed its final report and the matter is subjudice before the learned trial Court and the learned trial Court has also taken cognizance of the matter and also framed charges against the petitioner.
As such, this petition at this stage deserves to be quashed.

10. We have heard learned counsel for the parties, perused the pleadings and materials available on record, and with the consent of learned counsel appearing for the parties, the petition is being considered and decided finally at the admission stage itself.
11. From perusal of the FIR, it is evident that the incident of demand of illegal gratification is alleged to have taken in the year 2015-2016 and the FIR was lodged in the year 2021.

This Court, in Cr.M.P.
No. 1488/2023, vide order dated 13.11.2024, had quashed the FIR and the other consequential Ranjit Singh Saini vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22652290/
4 criminal proceedings against the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh on the ground that firstly, there was an inordinate delay of six years in lodging the FIR and secondly, the FIR was lodged only after change of the political regime in the State.
12.

sentences.text: No explanation has been offered by the complainant/respondent No. 5 as to what prevented him from lodging the FIR at the time of incident and what took him six long years to lodge the FIR against the petitioner and the other co-accused persons.

13. This Court had further observed that the facts and circumstances leading to the registration of the FIR clearly indicated that the criminal proceedings were initiated against the co-accused Gurjindar Pal Singh was instituted with ulterior motive for a malicious prosecution and as such, this Court had exercised its power under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. and quashed the FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings relying on the decisions of the Apex Court in Isaac Isanga Musumba and others v. State of Maharashtra, {(2014) 15 SCC 357, paragraph 3 and 7}, with respect to the issue of extortion, Hasmukhlal D. Vora v. State of T.N.,{(2022) 15 SCC 164, Para 23 to 27},
with respect to the issue of delay in lodging the FIR and the decision rendered in Ahmad Ali Quaraishi v. State of U.P. {(2020) 13 SCC 435, Para 13 to 19} with respect to power of theHigh Court under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C.
14.

sentences.text: No offence under Sections 388 or 506 of the IPC are made out even if the allegations in the FIR are taken on their face value.

The offence of extortion is not made out because there is no allegation in the FIR that the petitioner even put the complainant in any fear of any injury or induced him to deliver any valuable security.

Further, as per the averments made in the petition, the complainant himself is an accused in FIR bearing Crime No. 55/2018 dated 11.04.20189 registered at Police Station, Haripal, District Hoogly for the offences under Sections 420, 406, 409, 463, 464, 468, 471,
325, 326, 307, 308, 285, 286, 120-B, 34 of the IPC read with Section 3(a) of the Explosive Substances Act, 1908.
15.

In the present case, the FIR relating to extortion registered against the petitioner was lodged with a delay of six years and in this regard, the Supreme Court, in Hasmukhlal D. Vora (supra),
observed as under:
"23.
In the present case, the respondent has provided no explanation for the extraordinary delay of more than four years between the initial site inspection, the show cause notice, and the complaint.
In fact, the absence of such an explanation only prompts the Court to infer some sinister motive behind initiating the criminal proceedings.

24. While inordinate delay in itself may not be ground for quashing of a criminal complaint, in such cases, unexplained inordinate delay of such length must be taken into consideration as a very crucial factor as grounds for quashing a criminal complaint.

5 25.

sentences.text:
While this Court does not expect a full-blown investigation at the stage of a criminal complaint,however, in such cases where the accused has been subjected to the anxiety of a potential initiation of criminal proceedings for such a length of time,
it is only reasonable for the court to expect bare- minimum evidence from the Investigating Authorities.

26. At the cost of repetition, we again state that the purpose of filing a complaint and initiating criminal proceedings must exist solely to meet the ends of justice, and the law must not be used as a tool to harass the accused.
The law, is meant to exist as a shield to protect the innocent, rather than it being used as a sword to threaten them."

16. The Supreme Court, in State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal {(AIR 1992 Supreme Court 604}, has observed that where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge, the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. can be exercised.
17.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal {(AIR 1992 Supreme Court 604}
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since this Court has already quashed the FIR in respect of the co- accused Gurjindar Pal Singh against whom there were identical allegations, this Court is of the considered opinion that the same benefit should be extended to the petitioner herein also.

The petitioner herein is not holding any high post so as to make him competent enough to get the complainant/respondent No. 5 out of jail on bail in the criminal case pending against him and as such, the entire prosecution case appears to be forged and fabricated.

18. As a fallout of the above discussion, the FIR bearing Crime No. the FIR bearing Crime No.
590/2021, registered at Police Station Supela, District Durg, dated 27.07.2021, the charge-sheet No.
334/2022 dated 23.05.2022 and the consequential criminal proceedings being RCC No. 5193/2022,
including the order dated 27.05.2022 taking cognizance of the offence by the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Durg, and the order dated 12.03.2024 framing charge against the petitioner by the learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Durg, are hereby quashed.
19. Resultantly, this petition stands allowed.
